items.title: Orrin Keepnews interviewed by Monk Rowe, San Francisco, California, August 7, 2002
items.q: I sure have had a run of artists who never really believed that they have played it right. Who have to do another take because they didn’t get it yet, they haven’t done the best that they can do. And it’s amazing, I mean it’s a perfectly good description of Rollins, of Wes Montgomery

ctx.x: exactly how I learned to swim. And it was, I also will say that, I said it many years ago with what I have learned I would never entrust as valuable and volatile a commodity as Thelonious to anybody as totally ignorant and inexperienced as I was at the time. But fortunately one of the great advantages of that, well basically it’s a 1950s phenomenon primarily, it happened a little before that, it happened a little after that, but the idea of the jazz fan as self-made jazz record producer actually the art owes a…

about it, in which if not for me and the record company that I was operating and the way in which we proceeded with things — certainly a lot of careers would not have happened in the same way. I’m not saying that it wouldn’t have happened, but knowing what I do about — I’ll tell you, knowing what I do about some of the personalities that I dealt with I still haven’t figured out whether it was just luck of the draw or whether this is a more prevalent attitude than anybody appreciates but I sure have had a run of…
Let me ask you, what was in your childhood that steered you into jazz listening as a hobby first?

items.title: Orrin Keepnews — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: it’s Bill Evans and Wes Montgomery that stand out as an art. They are just a matter of my being told about somebody and having followed up on it.

ctx.x: Wes Montgomery. Yes. Actually, I guess when you’re putting things in order; it’s Bill Evans and Wes Montgomery that stand out as an art. They are just a matter of my being told about somebody and having followed up on it. That sequence of events thing that I was starting to talk to you about with the presence of Clark leading to the Adderely’s, and the really the next step in that story is Cannonball coming into my office one morning. He had just gotten back from a one-nighter in Indianapolis and telling me, “I…
Into Riverside, or Prestige? He came to your office?
